findings.element: "Key" field under Then refine (shown only after picking a metadata source) and the "Fix the highlighted fields" banner
findings.finding: Nothing marks the Key field as required when a metadata source is chosen; the user only learns it's mandatory after pressing Update and getting a generic "Fix the highlighted fields" banner with a small "Required" note buried in the row.
findings.user_impact: The user doesn't understand why saving failed or which of several fields is the problem, and is likely to give up on the custom setup rather than hunt for the highlighted field.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the Key field as required the moment a metadata source is picked (e.g. "Key (required)"), so the requirement is visible before submit, not only after a rejected save.

findings.element: Close (×) button, top-left of the "Payment matching rules" overlay header
findings.finding: Closing the overlay after changing a rule exits immediately with no "discard changes?" warning of any kind.
findings.user_impact: A user who closes by accident (or means to back out without losing everything) has no way to know their edits are gone until they reopen the panel later and find the old settings back, which reads as the tool losing their work.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a short confirmation ("Discard unsaved changes?") before closing whenever the draft differs from what was last saved.

findings.element: "Configure matching rules →" link under "Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions"
findings.finding: Turning the "Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions" switch off greys out "Configure matching rules →" with nothing on screen explaining why it just stopped working.
findings.user_impact: The user assumes the button, or the page, is broken and may reload or leave rather than realizing they need to switch "Apply payments" back on first.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short inline note next to the greyed-out link, e.g. "Turn on Apply payments above to edit matching rules."

gaps: Update (primary action) on a valid, error-free save: recon only exercised the blocked path (metadata source with an empty key). Whether a successful save gives visible confirmation a first-timer would notice (the "Matching rules updated" toast) was never recorded, so we can't confirm the save flow actually reassures the user their change stuck.
